results.name: person_session_drift_sd
results.description: SD across participants of (yes rate in second half of session minus first half, by trial_index); observed above null means individuals drift in yes-propensity over the session in different directions, which the model's constant per-person parameters cannot produce.
results.code:
# name: person_session_drift_sd
# description: SD across participants of (yes rate in second half of session minus first half, by trial_index); observed above null means individuals drift in yes-propensity over the session in different directions, which the model's constant per-person parameters cannot produce.
def test_statistic(df):
    ti = df["trial_index"].to_numpy()
    pid = np.cumsum(ti == 0)
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    d = pd.DataFrame({"pid": pid, "late": ti >= 225, "r": r})
    m = d.groupby(["pid", "late"])["r"].mean().unstack()
    diff = (m[True] - m[False]).dropna()
    if len(diff) < 2:
        return 0.0
    return float(diff.std(ddof=1))

results.name: cell_unanimity_rate
results.description: Fraction of distinct (number_set, target) cells (with >=5 responses) on which all responses agree (all yes or all no); observed above null means people agree more sharply per stimulus than the model's cell probabilities imply (model too graded/underconfident), below means too extreme.

results.name: cross_set_lag1_carryover
results.description: Within a participant (participants = runs starting at trial_index 0), P(yes | previous trial yes) minus P(yes | previous trial no), over consecutive trials whose number_set differs; observed above null means answers carry over between unrelated trials more than the model's independent per-trial responses (plus stable person bias) produce.
results.code:
# name: cross_set_lag1_carryover
# description: Within a participant (participants = runs starting at trial_index 0), P(yes | previous trial yes) minus P(yes | previous trial no), over consecutive trials whose number_set differs; observed above null means answers carry over between unrelated trials more than the model's independent per-trial responses (plus stable person bias) produce.
def test_statistic(df):
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    ti = df["trial_index"].to_numpy()
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str).to_numpy()
    pid = np.cumsum(ti == 0)
    ok = (pid[1:] == pid[:-1]) & (s[1:] != s[:-1])
    prev = r[:-1][ok]
    cur = r[1:][ok]
    if (prev == 1).sum() == 0 or (prev == 0).sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(cur[prev == 1].mean() - cur[prev == 0].mean())

results.name: first_encounter_of_set_yes
results.description: Yes rate on the trial where a participant first sees a given number_set minus yes rate on their later trials with that set; observed above null means first judgments about a set are more liberal (later ones stricter) than the model's order-free responding predicts, below null the reverse.
results.code:
# name: first_encounter_of_set_yes
# description: Yes rate on the trial where a participant first sees a given number_set minus yes rate on their later trials with that set; observed above null means first judgments about a set are more liberal (later ones stricter) than the model's order-free responding predicts, below null the reverse.
def test_statistic(df):
    ti = df["trial_index"].to_numpy()
    pid = np.cumsum(ti == 0)
    key = pd.Series(pid.astype(str)) + "|" + df["number_set"].astype(str).reset_index(drop=True)
    first = ~key.duplicated().to_numpy()
    multi = key.map(key.value_counts()).to_numpy() > 1
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    a, b = first & multi, (~first) & multi
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: digit_reversal_target
results.description: Yes rate for non-example targets that are the digit reversal of a two-digit example (e.g. 38 for 83) minus yes rate for other non-example targets sharing a digit with an example, averaged over in-span/out-of-span strata; observed above null means digit-anagram similarity drives generalization beyond the model's digit concepts.
results.code:
# name: digit_reversal_target
# description: Yes rate for non-example targets that are the digit reversal of a two-digit example (e.g. 38 for 83) minus yes rate for other non-example targets sharing a digit with an example, averaged over in-span/out-of-span strata; observed above null means digit-anagram similarity drives generalization beyond the model's digit concepts.
def test_statistic(df):
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    exl = ex.str.split(",")
    lo = exl.apply(lambda x: min(int(v) for v in x)).to_numpy()
    hi = exl.apply(lambda x: max(int(v) for v in x)).to_numpy()
    rev = exl.apply(lambda x: set(int(v[::-1]) for v in x if len(v) == 2 and v[1] != "0" and v[0] != v[1]))
    exset = exl.apply(lambda x: set(int(v) for v in x))
    isrev = np.array([a in s for a, s in zip(t, rev)])
    isex = np.array([a in s for a, s in zip(t, exset)])
    digs = ex.str.replace(",", "", regex=False)
    tstr = pd.Series(t).astype(str)
    share = np.zeros(len(df), dtype=bool)
    for dch in "0123456789":
        share |= (digs.str.contains(dch, regex=False).to_numpy() & tstr.str.contains(dch, regex=False).to_numpy())
    inspan = (t >= lo) & (t <= hi)
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    diffs = []
    for st in (True, False):
        m = (~isex) & (inspan == st)
        a, b = m & isrev, m & share & ~isrev
        if a.sum() >= 3 and b.sum() >= 3:
            diffs.append(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())
    return float(np.mean(diffs)) if diffs else 0.0

results.name: repdigit_target_salience
results.description: Among non-example targets sharing no digit with any example, yes rate for repdigit targets (11,22,...,99) minus non-repdigit targets, averaged over the in-span and out-of-span strata; observed above null means repdigits are endorsed as a salient category the model lacks.
results.code:
# name: repdigit_target_salience
# description: Among non-example targets sharing no digit with any example, yes rate for repdigit targets (11,22,...,99) minus non-repdigit targets, averaged over the in-span and out-of-span strata; observed above null means repdigits are endorsed as a salient category the model lacks.
def test_statistic(df):
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    exl = ex.str.split(",")
    lo = exl.apply(lambda x: min(int(v) for v in x)).to_numpy()
    hi = exl.apply(lambda x: max(int(v) for v in x)).to_numpy()
    digs = ex.str.replace(",", "", regex=False)
    tstr = pd.Series(t).astype(str)
    share = np.zeros(len(df), dtype=bool)
    for dch in "0123456789":
        share |= (digs.str.contains(dch, regex=False).to_numpy() & tstr.str.contains(dch, regex=False).to_numpy())
    isex = np.array([str(a) in b.split(",") for a, b in zip(t, ex)])
    rep = (t >= 11) & (t % 11 == 0)
    inspan = (t >= lo) & (t <= hi)
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    base = (~share) & (~isex)
    diffs = []
    for st in (True, False):
        m = base & (inspan == st)
        a, b = m & rep, m & ~rep
        if a.sum() >= 3 and b.sum() >= 3:
            diffs.append(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())
    return float(np.mean(diffs)) if diffs else 0.0

results.name: parity_match_out_of_span
results.description: For sets of >=2 examples that are all odd or all even, yes rate for out-of-span targets matching the examples' parity minus mismatching ones; observed above null means parity generalizes beyond the examples' span more than the model predicts (below null: less).
results.code:
# name: parity_match_out_of_span
# description: For sets of >=2 examples that are all odd or all even, yes rate for out-of-span targets matching the examples' parity minus mismatching ones; observed above null means parity generalizes beyond the examples' span more than the model predicts (below null: less).
def test_statistic(df):
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    exl = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",")
    n = exl.apply(len).to_numpy()
    odd_ct = exl.apply(lambda x: sum(int(v) % 2 for v in x)).to_numpy()
    lo = exl.apply(lambda x: min(int(v) for v in x)).to_numpy()
    hi = exl.apply(lambda x: max(int(v) for v in x)).to_numpy()
    pure = (n >= 2) & ((odd_ct == 0) | (odd_ct == n))
    setpar = (odd_ct == n).astype(int)
    out = (t < lo) | (t > hi)
    match = (t % 2) == setpar
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    a, b = pure & out & match, pure & out & ~match
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: scale_endpoint_targets
results.description: Yes rate for out-of-span targets 1 or 100 minus yes rate for all other out-of-span targets on the same sets; observed above null means the scale endpoints are endorsed as special/anchor numbers more than the model's concepts imply (below: less).
results.code:
# name: scale_endpoint_targets
# description: Yes rate for out-of-span targets 1 or 100 minus yes rate for all other out-of-span targets on the same sets; observed above null means the scale endpoints are endorsed as special/anchor numbers more than the model's concepts imply (below: less).
def test_statistic(df):
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    exl = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",")
    lo = exl.apply(lambda x: min(int(v) for v in x)).to_numpy()
    hi = exl.apply(lambda x: max(int(v) for v in x)).to_numpy()
    out = (t < lo) | (t > hi)
    end = (t == 1) | (t == 100)
    sets = df["number_set"].to_numpy()
    with_end = np.isin(sets, np.unique(sets[out & end]))
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    a, b = out & end, out & ~end & with_end
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())
